name: sprinty-mcp

tools.name: info
tools.description: Startup orientation and compact sprint discovery before binding to one sprint.

tools.name: sprint_new
tools.description: Start a sprint with explicit git_dir and a worktree-scoped, uncommitted data_dir; returns orientation.

tools.name: sprint_resume
tools.description: Resume an existing sprint by binding this MCP session to an existing git_dir and data_dir without creating a sprint.

tools.name: sprint_detach
tools.description: Detach this MCP session from its current Sprinty binding and stop the dashboard.

tools.name: sprint_close
tools.description: Re-check all gates, write the canonical SemVer changelog, and close the sprint; force bypasses only executable gate failures.

tools.name: sprint_archive
tools.description: Archive the sprint with a recovery reason, bypassing normal close gates.

tools.name: overview
tools.description: Compact sprint overview: title, details, notes, artifacts, and subsprint counts.

tools.name: next
tools.description: Compact work window for choosing the next item.

tools.name: subsprint_new
tools.description: Create a subsprint (description, goals, gates).

tools.name: subsprint_get
tools.description: Read one subsprint with compact item rows.

tools.name: subsprint_list
tools.description: List subsprints with compact rows.

tools.name: item_add
tools.description: Add an atomic item (bounded title, bounded description, code locations, gates — all required; gate_timeout_ms defaults to 5000 and null disables it).

tools.name: item_get
tools.description: Read one item with full untruncated detail.

tools.name: item_update
tools.description: Update an item by id: metadata, open-item gates/timeout, completed-item commit_id, and/or dependency ids.

tools.name: item_done
tools.description: Resolve an item as completed with a commit id and a semver changelog verb (added/fixed/changed/removed/deprecated/security). Sprinty runs the item's executable gates itself; only manual gates take agent-supplied gate_results.

tools.name: item_split
tools.description: Resolve an item as split, creating a seeded subsprint atomically.

tools.name: item_deprecate
tools.description: Resolve an item as deprecated with a reason, or drop a whole subsprint by passing its id (its open items are deprecated too).

tools.name: note_add
tools.description: Add a note to a specific item id. Notes are not substitutes for item_add(); create items for trackable work.

tools.name: note_get
tools.description: Read notes attached to an item id.

tools.name: note_list
tools.description: List notes for an item as compact rows.

tools.name: note_update
tools.description: Update a note by note id.

tools.name: artifact_add
tools.description: Attach a file path to the sprint, optionally related to item ids.

tools.name: artifact_get
tools.description: Read one artifact by id.

tools.name: artifact_list
tools.description: Page through active sprint artifacts as compact newest-first rows.

tools.name: artifact_update
tools.description: Update an artifact by id.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Regex search over sprint text with character context around each match.

tools.name: changelog
tools.description: Preview or export the current SemVer Markdown changelog and return only its path; sprint_close writes the canonical changelog automatically.

tools.name: dashboard_info
tools.description: Return the current dashboard URL and port without starting or restarting it.

tools.name: dashboard_restart
tools.description: Restart the follow-along dashboard and return its URL and port.

tools.name: agent_list
tools.description: List named agents, activity state and claim counts; paginated and token-free.

tools.name: items_claimed
tools.description: List current item claims, optionally only yours; includes timing, progress and stall reasons.

tools.name: agent_attach
tools.description: Attach an independent named agent; retain its returned token for shared connections.

tools.name: agent_detach
tools.description: Detach only this agent and release its claims.

tools.name: agent_heartbeat
tools.description: Report activity during long tasks; does not reset item progress or stall completion counts.

tools.name: item_claim
tools.description: Claim an open item. Optional force is a 1–500 character explanation that overrides existing ownership immediately, without activity or stall conditions; recorded in handover history.

tools.name: item_release
tools.description: Release your claim for another agent.

tools.name: item_takeover
tools.description: Take over a potentially stalled claim with an explanation, or pass force as a 1–500 character explanation to override ownership immediately without activity or stall conditions.

tools.name: item_progress
tools.description: Record meaningful progress on your claimed item.

instructions:
Sprinty enforces a disciplined sprint.
Call info() first for unbound startup orientation, compact sprint discovery, and the current dashboard state.
One sprint per explicit git/data binding. sprint_new and sprint_resume require git_dir; when data_dir is omitted, Sprinty uses <git_dir>/.sprinty and never guesses from the MCP process cwd.
Use a worktree-scoped, uncommitted data_dir, usually <git_dir>/.sprinty when it is gitignored; avoid shared temp dirs and committed sprint state.
The data_dir/current pointer keeps exactly one open sprint for that binding. After an MCP restart, call info({ git_dir }) or info({ workspace_dirs }) to inspect existing ledgers, then sprint_resume(git_dir, data_dir?) to reattach to an existing sprint without creating a new one. Use sprint_detach() to clear the process binding.
Call overview() after binding for compact sprint shape, or next() for the active work window.
Resume/create automatically attaches a named agent to this MCP connection; ordinary calls need no token. Native client session/subagent IDs recover identities automatically. Claude plugin hooks supply these IDs; agent_token remains an advanced fallback for other shared connections. Use agent_list and items_claimed({ mine:true }) to inspect ownership. Claim items with item_claim before editing or resolving them. Use agent_heartbeat during long tasks, item_progress for meaningful progress, and item_release or agent_detach to hand work back. Potential stalls require explicit item_takeover with a 1–500 character explanation; never assume a stall released ownership. For explicit recovery or reassignment, item_claim and item_takeover accept force as a 1–500 character explanation string; this overrides ownership immediately without inactivity or stall conditions. ETA uses observed activity, pauses without active agents, and learns after three claimed completions.
Build is item-driven: sprint_new(goal, git_dir, data_dir, context_notes?) -> dashboard URL for the human -> subsprint_new(..., dependencies?)
-> item_add(title + description + code_locations + gates, dependencies?) -> item_done(commit + changelog; Sprinty runs the executable gates itself under a 5s budget, only manual gates take gate_results)
| item_split(promote to a subsprint) | item_deprecate(reason). item_deprecate also accepts a subsprint id to drop a whole subsprint and its open items. Use item_update(id, ...) to replace open-item gates/timeout, correct a completed item's commit_id, or change dependency edges.
Each subsprint should be one feature. Notes attach only to item ids: use note_add(id, text), note_list(id), note_get(id), and note_update(id, text).
Use artifact_add/list/get/update for durable file outputs attached to the sprint, optionally related to item ids.
next() returns a compact work window, blocked item ids/titles, scoped relations, artifacts, and recent activity. It deliberately omits the full dependency graph.
item_done() records a Git-backed file change map and a semver changelog verb in the ledger; compact tool responses omit change maps. changelog({ path? }) previews or exports the current SemVer Markdown and returns only the path.
sprint_close writes the canonical data-dir changelog automatically after re-running executable gates;
it refuses to close if anything is open, uncommitted, missing an item changelog entry, missing coverage, or failing a gate. A subsprint left with no items is open work: give it items or drop it with item_deprecate. IDs are minted by the server.
Every response carries next_tools: concrete calls derived from live state, with ids that exist. sprint_resume returns a bounded briefing so state is recovered rather than re-derived.
Use search(pattern, context_size) to query the immutable record with bounded character context and focused tool_call hints. sprint_new and sprint_resume return a live dashboard URL; dashboard_info reports it and dashboard_restart refreshes it.
